implementation_notes: The .NET Golden Hammer is usually the Microsoft stack end to end, applied without a comparison — ASP.NET MVC for a UI that should be a desktop app, Entity Framework for a workload that is write-heavy and read-rare, LINQ to Entities in a hot path. EF is the sharpest case because it is genuinely excellent for the workloads it was designed for and genuinely wrong for high-volume writes, and the team rarely has the measurement that would tell them so. The local mitigation is to record query counts, round-trip counts and p99 latency as requirements and compare against one alternative data access approach before the choice hardens.
idiom_name: ASP.NET + EF Core applied to every problem shape
pitfalls: `SaveChanges` inside a loop is the EF Golden Hammer's signature failure and produces one round trip per entity.
AutoMapper profiles generated per entity type make the data-access choice a project-wide commitment made once.
Choosing ASP.NET because it is the platform the team knows, for an application whose natural shape is not a web request.
